Economic non-viability.

Until we have a working H3 fusion reactor or need a way point for solar/interstellar travel, there exists little legitimate reason to return to the moon aside from science. And all of that science can be achieved via remote methods. Be them robotics, sensors, or telescopes.

The next closest reason is asteroid mining. The moon may make a good processing center.

To ask the question, you really need to understand why we went to the moon in the first place. During the space race, we were in an ideological battle with the Soviets. More importantly, it was actually a guise to justify massive expense to create ICBMs (nuclear missiles). If you have the lift capability to launch a manned mission to the moon, you have the lift capability to launch a large nuclear payload for delivery to any place on the planet. This is especially important given the size of the original nuclear weapons. Worth mentioning, discussion of nuking the moon was seriously entertained so as to provide sufficient dick waving power to counter the Soviets.

Today, we have nuclear weapons. Today, we have no ideological villain. Which means the only reasons to go are science and economics. As I said, science can be done remotely. There is no real economic justification today - well, not immediately. The next closest ideological justification is that many other countries, including China and India are planning manned missions to the moon. As such, there is now renewed interest in US dick waving on the moon.

Realistically, outside of national pride and dick waving, there exists no legitimate reason to return to the moon unless we crank up asteroid mining or some other such economic endeavor.
